title: The integer residue model at a closed prime
statement: Let $p$ be a rational prime and set $\mathfrak p=p\mathbf Z$. Let $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)=\mathbf Z_{\mathfrak p}/p\mathbf Z_{\mathfrak p}$ be its residue field [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The map $\mathbf Z\to k$ is surjective with kernel $p\mathbf Z$, and it induces a ring isomorphism $\mathbf Z/p\mathbf Z\cong k$. For every finite purely inseparable field extension $j:k\to L$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], the map $j$ is surjective. Put $B=\operatorname{im}(\mathbf Z\to k\xrightarrow{j}L)$ with its induced $\mathbf Z$-algebra structure. Then $B=L$ as subrings of $L$; $B$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and finite as a $\mathbf Z$-module, generated by $1$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]; every element of $L$ is $b/c$ with $b,c\in B$ and $c\ne0$; and $\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is nonempty, with $B_{\mathfrak q}$ regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme] for every prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B$. Thus its whole spectrum is a nonempty regular open subset.

source.place: Tag 07PJ, proposition-ubiquity-J-2, proof of case (3), verification of condition (4) of lemma-J-2: the nonzero-prime regular finite model: residue-field identification, Frobenius calculation, triviality of the extension, and regular field model (returned proof Step 4).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-z-localizations-dvr], $(p)$ is prime and the maximal ideal of $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ is $p\mathbf Z_{(p)}$; [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] identifies $k$ with its quotient by this ideal and represents elements by classes of fractions $a/s$ with $p\nmid s$. For such an $s$, choose the least positive integer $d=us+vp$ among the integer linear combinations of $s,p$ (this set contains $p>0$). Division with remainder shows that $d$ divides both $s$ and $p$: a nonzero remainder would be a smaller positive linear combination. Since $p$ is prime, $d$ is $1$ or $p$, and $p\nmid s$ excludes the latter. Thus $us+vp=1$. Now $a/s-au=avp/s$ belongs to $p\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, so every residue class is represented by an integer. This proves surjectivity of $\mathbf Z\to k$.

source.place: Tag 07PJ (proposition-ubiquity-J-2), case (3), closed-prime verification of Tag 07PC condition (4); explicit integer division and fraction calculation

proof.text: The kernel contains $p\mathbf Z$. Conversely, if $t\in\mathbf Z$ maps to zero, then $t/1=pa/s$ for integers $a,s$ with $p\nmid s$: every element of the ideal generated by $p$ has this form. The fraction equality in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] gives $w(st-pa)=0$ for some integer $w$ not divisible by $p$, so $st=pa$. Take $u,v$ as in Step 1 for this $s$. Then $t=(us+vp)t=p(ua+vt)$, and $p\mid t$. Hence the kernel is exactly $p\mathbf Z$. The map $e:\mathbf Z/p\mathbf Z\to k$, $[a]\mapsto[a/1]$, is well defined and preserves ring operations. It is surjective by Step 1 and injective by the kernel equality. Its set-theoretic inverse preserves addition, multiplication and $1$, by applying the injective map $e$ to each required equality. Thus $e$ is a ring isomorphism. In particular $p\cdot1=0$ in $k$ and $L$, and their characteristic is exactly $p$: a smaller positive characteristic would divide the prime $p$, forcing $1=0$.

source.place: Tag 07PJ (proposition-ubiquity-J-2), case (3); explicit kernel and quotient-isomorphism verification

proof.text: Use [def-weil-ring-frobenius] on the characteristic-$p$ field $L$: the map $F^n:z\mapsto z^{p^n}$ is a unital ring endomorphism for every $n\ge0$. It therefore fixes every integer multiple of $1$. By Step 1 each $a\in k$ is such a multiple, so $F^n(j(a))=j(a)$. For $x\in L$, [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] supplies $n\ge0$ and $a\in k$ with $x^{p^n}=j(a)$. Additivity of $F^n$ now gives $(x-j(a))^{p^n}=j(a)-j(a)=0$. The exponent is positive, and a nonzero field element has nonzero powers (multiply by its inverse power), so $x=j(a)$. Thus $j$ is surjective. This argument includes $n=0$, where $F^0$ is the identity; finiteness of the given extension is not needed for surjectivity.

source.place: Tag 09HE (definition-purely-inseparable), applied to the prime field; Frobenius is the ring map of Varieties Tag 03SM (definition-absolute-frobenius), following paragraph

proof.text: The two surjections $\mathbf Z\to k$ and $j:k\to L$ show that their composite has image the full subring $L$; hence the specified $B$ equals $L$ as subrings. Explicitly every $b\in B$ is the image of an integer $m$, so $b=m\cdot1_B$ for the prescribed $\mathbf Z$-action. Thus $\{1_B\}$ generates $B$ as a $\mathbf Z$-module, which is finiteness in [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Every $x\in L=B$ is $x/1$ with numerator and denominator in $B$ and $1\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 07PJ (proposition-ubiquity-J-2), case (3), finite residue-field model; explicit image, module generator and fraction witnesses

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-field-regular-ring] to the field $B=L$: it is Noetherian and its only prime localization is regular local. These are precisely the properties defined in [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and [def-weil-regular-scheme]. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the spectrum of a field has one point; in particular it is nonempty. Its whole space is open. Thus $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ is the required nonempty regular open, with $B_{\mathfrak q}$ regular local at every prime.

lean.statement: theorem integers_closed_residue_model (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] : Function.Surjective (algebraMap ℤ (Ideal.span {(p : ℤ)}).ResidueField) ∧ RingHom.ker (algebraMap ℤ (Ideal.span {(p : ℤ)}).ResidueField) = Ideal.span {(p : ℤ)} ∧ (∃ e : (ℤ ⧸ Ideal.span {(p : ℤ)}) ≃+* (Ideal.span {(p : ℤ)}).ResidueField, ∀ a : ℤ, e (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {(p : ℤ)}) a) = algebraMap ℤ (Ideal.span {(p : ℤ)}).ResidueField a) ∧ ∀ (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra (Ideal.span {(p : ℤ)}).ResidueField L] [Module.Finite (Ideal.span {(p : ℤ)}).ResidueField L] [IsPurelyInseparable (Ideal.span {(p : ℤ)}).ResidueField L], Function.Surjective (algebraMap (Ideal.span {(p : ℤ)}).ResidueField L) ∧ ∀ B : Subring L, B = ((algebraMap (Ideal.span {(p : ℤ)}).ResidueField L).comp (algebraMap ℤ (Ideal.span {(p : ℤ)}).ResidueField)).range → B = ⊤ ∧ IsNoetherianRing B ∧ Module.Finite ℤ B ∧ Submodule.span ℤ ({(1 : B)} : Set B) = ⊤ ∧ (∀ x : L, ∃ b c : B, (c : L) ≠ 0 ∧ x = (b : L) / (c : L)) ∧ Nonempty (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of B)) ∧ (∀ (q : Ideal B) [q.IsPrime], IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime q)) ∧ AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegularScheme (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of B))
